{{Short description|Mathematical functor in representation theory and algebraic topology}}
In [[mathematics]], particularly in [[representation theory]] and [[algebraic topology]], a '''Mackey functor''' is a type of [[functor]] that generalizes various constructions in [[group theory]] and [[Equivariant stable homotopy theory|equivariant homotopy theory]]. Named after [[Americans|American]] [[mathematician]] [[George Mackey]], these functors were first introduced by [[Germans|German]] mathematician [[Andreas Dress]] in 1971.<ref name="dress">{{cite report
| last1=Dress | first1=A. W. M. | authorlink1=Andreas Dress
| date=1971
| title=Notes on the theory of representations of finite groups. Part I: The Burnside ring of a finite group and some AGN-applications
| location=Bielefeld}}</ref><ref name="nlab">{{cite web|url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Mackey+functor|title=Mackey functor|website=[[nLab]]|access-date=January 3, 2025}}</ref>

==Definition==
===Classical definition===
Let <math>G</math> be a [[finite group]]. A Mackey functor <math>M</math> for <math>G</math> consists of:
* For each [[subgroup]] <math>H \leq G</math>, an [[abelian group]] <math>M(H)</math>,
* For each pair of subgroups <math>H, K \leq G</math> with <math>H \subseteq K</math>:
** A [[restriction (mathematics)|restriction homomorphism]] <math>R^K_H: M(K) \to M(H)</math>,
** A [[transfer (group theory)|transfer homomorphism]] <math>I^K_H: M(H) \to M(K)</math>.
These maps must satisfy the following axioms:
:'''Functoriality''': For nested subgroups <math>H \subseteq K \subseteq L</math>, <math>R^L_H = R^K_H \circ R^L_K</math> and <math>I^L_H = I^L_K \circ I^K_H</math>.
:'''Conjugation''': For any <math>g \in G</math> and <math>H \leq G</math>, there are [[isomorphisms]] <math>c_g: M(H) \to M(gHg^{-1})</math> compatible with restriction and transfer.
:'''[[Double coset]] formula''': For subgroups <math>H, K \leq G</math>, the following identity holds:
::<math>R^G_H I^G_K = \sum_{x \in [H\backslash G/K]} I^H_{H \cap xKx^{-1}} \circ c_x \circ R^K_{x^{-1}Hx \cap K}</math>.<ref name="dress"/>
===Modern definition===
In modern [[category theory]], a Mackey functor can be defined more elegantly using the language of [[span (category theory)|spans]]. Let <math>\mathcal{C}</math> be a disjunctive [[quasi-category]] and <math>\mathcal{A}</math> be an additive quasi-category. A Mackey functor is a [[product-preserving functor]] <math>M: \text{Span}(\mathcal{C}) \to \mathcal{A}</math> where <math>\text{Span}(\mathcal{C})</math> is the quasi-category of correspondences in <math>\mathcal{C}</math>.<ref name="barwick">{{cite journal
| last1=Barwick | first1=Clark | author-link1=Clark Barwick
| date=2017
| title=Spectral Mackey functors and equivariant algebraic K-theory (I)
| journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]
| volume=304
| pages=646–727
| doi=10.1016/j.aim.2016.08.043 | doi-access=free| hdl=20.500.11820/9eb49b0b-e23f-4b04-9aee-b44c6189ff21
| hdl-access=free
}}</ref>

==Applications==
===In equivariant homotopy theory===
Mackey functors play an important role in [[equivariant stable homotopy theory]]. For a genuine <math>G</math>-spectrum <math>E</math>, its equivariant homotopy groups form a Mackey functor given by:
:<math>\pi_n(E): G/H \mapsto [G/H_+ \wedge S^n, X]^G</math>
where <math>[-,-]^G</math> denotes [[morphisms]] in the equivariant stable homotopy category.<ref name="may">{{cite book
| last1=May | first1=J. P. |author-link1=J. Peter May
| date=1996
| title=Equivariant homotopy and cohomology theory
| series=CBMS Regional Conference Series in Mathematics
| volume=91
| publisher=American Mathematical Society}}</ref>

===Cohomology with Mackey functor coefficients===
For a pointed G-CW complex <math>X</math> and a Mackey functor <math>A</math>, one can define [[equivariant]] [[cohomology]] with coefficients in <math>A</math> as:
:<math>H^n_G(X,A) := H^n(\text{Hom}(C_\bullet(X), A))</math>
where <math>C_\bullet(X)</math> is the [[chain complex]] of Mackey functors given by stable equivariant [[homotopy group]]s of [[Quotient space (topology)|quotient spaces]].<ref name="kronholm">{{cite journal
| last1=Kronholm | first1=William C.
| date=2010
| title=The RO(G)-graded Serre spectral sequence
| journal=Homology, Homotopy and Applications
| volume=12
| issue=1
| pages=75-92
| url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/homology-homotopy-and-applications/volume-12/issue-1/The-ROG-graded-Serre-spectral-sequence/hha/1296223823.full}}</ref>
